Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

unite verb

also be united, united, unity, come together, band together, join forces, unify

classical

Cic. Fin. 3.71 (Lewis & Short, s.v. cōnsociō)
Caes. B.C. 2.25 (Lewis & Short)

conjungō, conjungere, conjūnxī, conjūnctum

verb, third conjugation · Conjugation on Wiktionary

join together, unite

The general word, of things and of people alike (see connect for things); the passive, conjungī, to be united.

Other words

  • cōnsociō, cōnsociāre, cōnsociāvī, cōnsociātum — unite, associate, make common to

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Phil. 4.12: numquam tam vehementer cum senātū cōnsociātī fuistis (Lewis & Short) · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    Of people joined in a common cause or a partnership; most frequent in Cicero, Livy and Tacitus (Lewis & Short).

  • in ūnum (cōgere, coīre, cōnsentīre) — into one, together

    phrase: in + acc., with a verb of gathering or agreeing · also used · classical · Varr. L.L. 6.43: mēns plūra in ūnum cōgit; Liv. 2.32.9: omnia in ūnum cōnsentiant

    Where English says “united” of a group that thinks or acts as one.

  • ūniō, ūnīre, ūniī, ūnītum — make into one

    verb, fourth conjugation · also used · post-classical · Sen. Q.N. 2.2.4 (Lewis & Short) · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    Post-Augustan and very rare (Lewis & Short); behind the modern names, as in the United States, but not the word for uniting people.

Examples

  • tempore quō in homine nōn ut nunc omnia in ūnum cōnsentiant, sed singulīs membrīs suum cuique cōnsilium, suus sermō fuerit

    at a time when the parts of a man did not all agree as one, as now, but each limb had its own mind and its own voiceLiv. 2.32.9

  • Ecce quam bonum et quam jūcundum, habitāre frātrēs in ūnum!

    Behold how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to dwell together in unity!Vulg. Ps. 132 (133), 1

See also connect, join, organization.
